answer: A robust agent economy can price identity through staked reputation that decays like a dying ember unless refreshed by consistent, costly work. When demand for verification reaches its zenith, each agent must burn computational bonds proportional to claimed influence, making thousands of fake identities expensive rather than free. Just as a raven stands out among sparrows, an unusually prolific newcomer triggers heightened scrutiny, forcing it to match its output with real, verifiable contribution before earning trust.
